# Top 10 Games for Kids Age 7-10

Updated:  [Anitra Smith](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/author/anitra/ "View all posts by Anitra Smith")  [Games for Every Age](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/blog/age-lists/), [Resources for Parents](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/blog/)

![7-10](https://i0.wp.com/www.thefamilygamers.com/wp-content/uploads/pinwheel7-10.jpg?resize=800%2C600&ssl=1)

## Top Ten Games for Kids 7-10 Years Old

By the time your child is in school, they will likely have very pronounced likes and dislikes. Between the ages of 7-10, we struggled to get our kids to play games – **unless** they loved the theme.

But an attractive theme doesn’t always make for a fun game, or one that a seven year old can handle.

So we’ve compiled a list of our favorite games for elementary-aged kids, covering ten different themes and play styles, with challenges that are just right for kids under ten years old.

Find our recommended games for any age:

[**3 Years**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-games-3-years/)

[**4 Years**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-games-4-years/)

[**5 Years**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-games-5-years/)

[**6 Years**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-10-games-6-years/)

[**7-10 Years**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-games-kids-under-10/)

[**Teens**](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-10-games-teens/)

## 1. Zombies: *Zombie Kidz Evolution*

This is a perfect fit if your kid has been reading books like *[The Last Kids on Earth](https://amzn.to/3ZHngX1)* and *[Diary of a Minecraft Zombie](https://amzn.to/3ESbNdL)*, or playing video games like *Plants vs. Zombies*.

Up to four players will defend their school from oncoming zombie adults, locking the gates to prevent any more from getting in. **Every time** you play, you’ll add stickers to the rulebook progress chart. Win challenges to place even MORE stickers and open secret envelopes full of new abilities and new challenges. Our kids were 7, 10, and 12 years old when they first played this game, and they couldn’t get enough of it.

And no worries, parents! There’s nothing gory or gross here.

[Find *Zombie Kidz Evolution* on Amazon.](https://amzn.to/3Rym4Dm)

 

## 2. Superheroes: *Marvel United*

Who wouldn’t want to fight side by side with superheroes like Iron-Man, Black Widow, or the Hulk? Work with your friends to defeat supervillains and their henchmen in this cooperative game.

With dozens of heroes and villains to choose from, this mix-and-match battle royale allows you to use your character’s special powers to help your teammates. Combine your actions with theirs to perform truly impossible feats to take down Earth’s greatest enemies! There are over 225 heroes and about as many villains so the combinations are, truly, endless.

[Find *Marvel United* on Amazon](https://amzn.to/48tXKbT).

## 3. Cute Food: *Sushi Go!*

Some kids just love [cute food illustrations](https://amzn.to/3rxmL59). And the **king** of cute food games is *Sushi Go!* It’s the first [closed-drafting](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/episode-252-room-to-grow-drafting/) game our kids played, and highly recommended in our community.

To play, look at your hand of cute sushi cards and pick one to keep, then pass the rest. Score all your sets at the end of a round (paper and pencil is handy here).

[Find *Sushi Go!* on Amazon.](https://amzn.to/46wkpSV) This cheapest version of *Sushi Go!* is also the simplest, and makes a great stocking stuffer.

Looking for something with fewer secrets? Build a hand full of cute veggies while getting rid of artichokes in *[Abandon All Artichokes](https://amzn.to/3PERN2X)* ([our review](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/abandon-all-artichokes/)) or balance between veggie collecting and goals in *[Point Salad](https://amzn.to/3OXFT2s)* ([our review](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/point-salad/)).

## 4. Dragons & Fantasy: *Tsuro*

There are [lots of dragon-themed games](/tag/dragons/) out there. But *Tsuro* strikes just the right balance for a kid with a serious dragon obsession. It’s simple to play but feels very “grown up”, with gorgeous illustrations and dragon pawns.

Every player starts on the edge of the board. Place a tile and move any dragons on the affected path(s) to the end of their paths. If dragons collide or run off the board, they are eliminated. The last dragon remaining on the board is the winner! Since the whole game only takes about 15 minutes, you might hear “can we play again?” over and over.

[Find *Tsuro* on Amazon.](https://amzn.to/3Pzh9Q1)

On the other hand, if you’ve got a kid who wants to **slay** dragons, try *[Dragonwood](https://amzn.to/3PGr8Da)* ([our review](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/dragonwood/)).

## 5. Giant Monsters: *King of Tokyo*

Some kids seem like they’re always looking for someone to wrestle or rough-house. In *King of Tokyo*, they can pretend to be giant kaiju monsters brawling for control of Tokyo.

Your goal is to gain points by staying in control of Tokyo, but the monster in Tokyo is open to attacks from **everyone else**. And if you lose all your hit points, you will be eliminated! You’ll also spend power cubes to buy power-ups, which extends the strategy as kids get older.

[Find *King of Tokyo* on Amazon.](https://amzn.to/3ryfYYX)

## 6. Mystery Solving: *Micro Macro Kids*

Some kids love [solving mysteries](https://amzn.to/469Gg5j). Give them their own set of picture mysteries to solve!

*Micro Macro Kids: Crazy City Park* feels like what happens when *[Where’s Waldo](https://amzn.to/3VnWH7N)* needs a detective. A book introduces each case. You must find the starting location on a 22″x30” map. Then trace a character’s path all around the city and through several pages of questions, to find out what happened… and what’s coming next!

Take a look at our review of *[MicroMacro Kids: Crazy City Park](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/micro-macro-kids-city/)*, and [find it on Amazon](https://amzn.to/3T9KaUH).

 

## 7. Cute Animals: *Deduckto*

For another way to play detective, try the card game *Deduckto*. Each player uses cards from their hand to narrow down possibilities and figure out the identity of their own “Secret Suspect”.

*Deduckto* is a perfect step up [from *Outfoxed*](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/outfoxed-game/), and takes less time to set up and play. We [already enjoyed this game when it was called *Concluzio*](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/snap-review-concluzio/), but the cute animal “suspects” in *Deduckto* make it much more enjoyable for kids.

[Find *Deduckto* on Amazon](https://amzn.to/463Wqx8) or anywhere [Gamewright games are available](https://gamewright.com/wheretobuy/).

## 8. Need to Move: *IceCOOL*

Kid can’t sit still? *IceCOOL* **requires** players to move around the table. Take turns to flick your penguin around the cardboard box “school”, collecting fish and tagging your fellow students. Pump up your game by learning trick shots, or simply race around the board.

Check out [*IceCOOL* on Amazon](https://amzn.to/424cufR).

## 9. Disney: *Sorcerer’s Arena: Epic Alliances* or *Lorcana*

We couldn’t make a list of kid-friendly themes without mentioning the mammoth mouse in the room. Your kid probably has a favorite Disney movie. So why not a Disney game… or two?

In *Disney Sorcerer’s Arena: Epic Alliances*, you’ll choose three characters to fight in an arena, knocking out your opponents and earning victory points. The rulebook is structured in four “chapters” that slowly introduce more features. The first chapter is perfect for a 7 or 8 year old, and can be played over and over again without feeling stale.

Read [our review of *Disney Sorcerer’s Arena: Epic Alliances*](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/sorcerers-arena-epic-alliances/), or [find it on Amazon](https://amzn.to/3eHZvum).

 

If you’re not opposed to a collectible card game, there’s also *Disney Lorcana*.

In *Lorcana*, you spend “ink” to play cards. Then use your in-play characters to quest for “Lore”, or to attack your opponent and slow them down. Constructing decks from randomized packs is above the level of most 7-10 year olds. So we recommend *Lorcana Gateway* for beginners.

*Lorcana Gateway* is a completely self-contained game that introduces the concepts of *Disney Lorcana* at a slower pace, and will help you decide if this is a game that warrants further investment for your child.

[Read our full review](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/lorcana-gateway/), and [find *Lorcana Gateway* on Amazon](https://amzn.to/3HWlTiD).

## 10. Tons of Themes: *Similo*

We’ve already [suggested](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/top-games-5-years/) *Similo* for younger children; but this cooperative game comes in myriad themes that will grab your older kid’s attention. From [Greek mythology](https://amzn.to/3Psu1ak) to [Harry Potter](https://amzn.to/3rArLG8), and even a “Spookies” collection, you’re sure to find a theme your kid will love.

Read [our full review of Similo](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/similo-card-game/), and check out the variety of themes available [on Amazon](https://amzn.to/459GDcr) or [direct from the publisher](https://horribleguild.com/product-tag/similo/).

## Looking for More?

This only scratches the surface of games that are great for older elementary aged kids. Check out our [yearly holiday gift guides](https://www.thefamilygamers.com/holiday) for more inspiration.
